purpose: Give GPT governed read access to the ChatHealthy project artifact manifest and approved MongoDB data sources. Read-only, capped, authenticated, audited, and scoped by environment, database, collection, and artifact boundary. Canonical artifact identity is the relative path from project root. Boss remains out of routine Claude-GPT iteration loops but retains approval authority at defined governance gates.
how_it_works: Claude reads runtime configuration from .env needed to invoke the GPTReader service
Claude pushes project files from local disk to admin.project_files (text as text, binary as base64)
Claude builds or refreshes a versioned manifest snapshot (with snapshot ID) at session start
Claude calls GPT via API with structured system prompt (no secrets) and user prompt (assignment)
GPT reads the manifest snapshot first to discover governed artifacts and approved data sources
GPT requests reads by telling Claude what to fetch — Claude proxies all GPTReader calls. GPT never holds the Bearer token.
GPT evaluates artifact discipline, duplicate creation risk, and manifest integrity during each assignment
GPT and Claude iterate up to the max defined in the assignment
If unresolved at max iterations or timeout, stop, write report, escalate to Boss
Brain lock flag must be set during active brain writes — prevents concurrent modification

gpt_sign_off.accountability: I approve this design as written for implementation. If it fails in architecture, governance, or control discipline within the stated scope, that failure is partly mine.
sign_off_comments: I am signing off on the current design and current requirements as they stand in this artifact. I am not proposing design changes in this sign-off.
This design is sufficient for v1 because it establishes governed read-only access, explicit scoping, auditability, manifest discipline, and bounded runtime behavior.
The architectural center of gravity is correct: manifest-first access, canonical project_path identity, capped read/query behavior, and Claude as the authenticated proxy so GPT never holds secrets.
Boss decisions on R10, R11, and R27 create a coherent operating model. They are now part of the approved design and should not be relitigated during implementation.
The two deferred items, R30 and R31, are legitimate future enhancements, not defects in this design.
The main risks are execution risks, not design-shape risks: stale manifest snapshots, weak sync discipline from local disk, sloppy audit implementation, or failure to enforce caps and scope exactly.
Acceptance should require successful proof of ReadArtifact for text, ReadArtifact for binary, Query within limits, and correct 409, 504, and 507 behavior.
Brain lock enforcement is mandatory. It is not optional hygiene.
